title: Design Stewards: Contribution Gateway & Sunset Protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description: Establish a compact, enforceable contribution gateway and a clear sunset protocol for visual tokens, core components (buttons, tables, charts), and adapter layers. This ticket codifies who can propose changes, how proposals are reviewed, the automated checks required, and the staged deprecation path when we retire tokens or components so consumer teams can migrate with minimal disruption.
contribution_flow: 1) Proposal intake: Contributors open a RFC-style PR in the design repo using template: /docs/rfcs/design-contrib-template.md and add label 'design-rfc'.

2) Automation checks: PR CI must run: token-lint, contrast-suite, snapshot-regression, and visual-diff for components. Bot assigns 'design-bot' reviewer if checks pass failure thresholds are exceeded triggers a blocker flag.

3) Triage meeting: Weekly triage (Design Stewards) evaluates scope, breaking risk, and rollout strategy within 3 business days. Outcome recorded as: accept | request-changes | schedule-for-deprecation.
4) Stakeholder review: Notify owners in OWNERS.yml (platform, SDKs, docs). For changes to tokens or public props, require at least one PM and one engineering approver.
5) Canary & experiments: Non-breaking opt-in changes can be merged behind a feature flag and released to dedicated projects for 2 release cycles before full rollout.
6) Final signoff & changelog: Merge only after all reviewers approve and changelog entry added to /CHANGELOG/design-system.md with migration guidance.
7) Post-merge monitoring: Instrument telemetry points for 4 weeks and validate no regressions in the console dashboards (error rates, CSS mismatch, token usage drift).
review_checklist: Design rationale: Does the RFC state the problem, alternatives considered, and measurable success criteria?
Compatibility: Are legacy token aliases provided or a clear migration mapping supplied?
Accessibility: Contrast, keyboard behavior, focus states, and screen-reader labels verified?
Performance: Any runtime cost (render time, bundle size) and suggested mitigations?
Testing: Unit + visual snapshot + accessibility automated tests included?
Docs: Usage examples, migration notes, and Console screenshots added to docs site?
Release: Is rollout strategy defined (feature flag, canary percentage, timeline)?
Deps: Dependencies and impacted consumer teams listed with contact points?
Ownership: Component owner updated and OWNERS.yml entry present?
Telemetry: Relevant metrics and dashboards requested via infra-monitoring ticket?
deprecation_policy: Stage 0 — Proposal to Deprecate: Design Stewards file a Deprecation RFC with migration plan and compatibility adapters (90-day minimum notice).
Stage 1 — Deprecated (soft): Mark token/component as 'deprecated' in docs and add runtime alias layer for 180 days. Create codemods for JS/TS consumers.
Stage 2 — Sunset window: After 180 days, schedule a removal release window; send cross-org notices to Consumer Owners and Customer Success for externally visible APIs (30 days pre-removal).
Stage 3 — Removal: Remove implementation but keep a shim package for one additional release if technically feasible; record final removal in CHANGELOG and migration guide.
Exceptions: Critical security fixes can bypass notice windows but must include a follow-up RFC explaining rationale and compensating migration helpers.
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal canary across 2 internal products and Redwood Console (2 weeks).
Phase B: Opt-in beta for external dedicated customers via config flag (1 month).
Phase C: Full rollout gated by telemetry (no >5% regression in render times and no accessibility violations).
Rollback plan: Revert flag or reintroduce alias mapping; communication template prepared for status page and release notes.
monitoring_and_metrics: Token adoption: % of repos using old token alias vs new token (weekly).
Visual regressions: Number of visual-diff failures post-merge (goal: 0).
Accessibility: Automated axe violations and manual audit findings logged per release.
Performance: Median render time for component across common viewports; bundle-size delta (bytes).
Incidents: Any bug or outage attributed to change recorded in Incident Board with roll-forward/rollback timeframe.
